```{r}
#| warning: false
library(tidyverse)
library(car)
library(broom)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(reactable)
library(plotly)
library(crosstalk)
library(leaps)
```


```{r}
credit <- read.csv("credit_risk_dataset.csv", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
credit_clean <- na.omit(credit)
credit_clean <- credit |>
  na.omit() |>
  filter(person_age <= 100)
reactable(credit, defaultPageSize = 4, searchable = TRUE)
```

```{r}
grade_query <- credit_clean |>
  group_by(loan_grade, cb_person_default_on_file) |>
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    mean_loan_int_rate = round(mean(loan_int_rate), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(loan_grade, cb_person_default_on_file)

reactable(grade_query, defaultPageSize = 7, searchable = TRUE)

# Assisted Visualization with AI

grade_plot_df <- grade_query |>
  mutate(
    default_label = ifelse(cb_person_default_on_file == "Y", "Prior Default on File", "No Prior Default"),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>Loan Grade:</b> ", loan_grade, "<br>",
      "<b>Status:</b> ", default_label, "<br>",
      "<b>Avg Interest Rate:</b> ", mean_loan_int_rate, "%<br>",
      "<b>Borrower Count:</b> ", scales::comma(count)
    )
  )

overall_avg <- round(mean(credit_clean$loan_int_rate), 2)

p1_pretty <- ggplot(
  grade_plot_df,
  aes(x = loan_grade, y = mean_loan_int_rate, fill = default_label, text = hover_text)
) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.78), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.92) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(mean_loan_int_rate, "%")),
    position = position_dodge(width = 1.5),
    vjust = 10,
    size = 3.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#2C3E50"
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = overall_avg, linetype = "dashed", color = "#7F8C8D", linewidth = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("No Prior Default" = "#2B5C8F", "Prior Default on File" = "#D95F02")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Loan Interest Rate by Loan Grade & Prior Default",
    x = "Loan Grade (A = Lowest Risk  →  G = Highest Risk)",
    y = "Average Loan Interest Rate (%)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12, color = "#1A2530", margin = margin(b = 12)),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#2C3E50"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#34495E", size = 11),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#ECF0F1"),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

ggplotly(p1_pretty, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = paste0(
        "<b>Average Loan Interest Rate by Loan Grade & Prior Default</b><br>"
      ),
      x = 0.02
    ),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0.02, y = 1.03, title = list(text = "")),
    margin = list(t = 85)
  )

```


```{r}
age_intent_query <- credit_clean |>
  mutate(
    age_group = case_when(
      person_age <= 25 ~ "18–25",
      person_age <= 35 ~ "26–35",
      person_age <= 45 ~ "36–45",
      TRUE ~ "46+"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(loan_intent, age_group) |>
  summarise(
    count = n(),
    avg_loan_int_rate = round(mean(loan_int_rate), 2),
    avg_age = round(mean(person_age), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(avg_loan_int_rate))


reactable(age_intent_query, defaultPageSize = 8, searchable = TRUE)

```

```{r}
age_trend <- credit_clean |>
  mutate(
    intent_clean = case_when(
      loan_intent == "DEBTCONSOLIDATION" ~ "Debt Consolidation",
      loan_intent == "HOMEIMPROVEMENT" ~ "Home Improvement",
      TRUE ~ str_to_title(loan_intent)
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(person_age, intent_clean) |>
  summarise(
    avg_rate = round(mean(loan_int_rate), 2),
    count = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>Age:</b> ", person_age, "<br>",
      "<b>Intent:</b> ", intent_clean, "<br>",
      "<b>Avg Rate:</b> ", avg_rate, "%<br>",
      "<b>Borrowers:</b> ", count
    )
  )

p_lines <- ggplot(
  age_trend,
  aes(x = person_age, y = avg_rate, color = intent_clean, group = intent_clean, text = hover_text)
) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = intent_clean), method = "loess", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(8, 15)) +
  labs(
    title = "Loan Interest Rate Across Borrower Age via Loan Purpose",
    x = "Age ",
    y = "Average Loan Interest Rate",
    color = "Loan Intent"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, color = "#1A2530"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#2C3E50"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

ggplotly(p_lines, tooltip = "text")


```
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
We see that these two factors, age and loan purpose are weak factors in determining the loan interest rate.
Now, let's make our model to see which factors are the most important.
:::

```{r}
credit_setup_df <- credit_clean |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

full_model <- lm(
  loan_int_rate ~ person_age + person_income + person_home_ownership + person_emp_length + loan_intent + loan_grade + loan_amnt + loan_percent_income + cb_person_default_on_file + cb_person_cred_hist_length,
  data = credit_setup_df
)
```

```{r}
current_model <- full_model

repeat {
  worst <- tidy(drop1(current_model, test = "F")) |>
    filter(!is.na(p.value), p.value > 0.05) |>
    slice_max(p.value, n = 1)
  
  if (nrow(worst) == 0) break
  
  current_model <- update(current_model, paste(". ~ . -", worst$term))
}

# Clean tidyverse summary table of the final model
final_summary <- tidy(current_model) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 4)))

```
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
This model has the factors that are statistically significant. However since the dataset is so large (n=29,000), some of these factors are quite practically insignificant.


For example, we discovered person_age is a weak factor in determining the loan_int_rate, because it's practically insignificant, but it's a statistically significant factor.
:::

$$
\begin{aligned}
{\text{loan\_int\_rate}} &= 7.3674 - 0.0051(\text{person\_age}) - 0.00000018(\text{person\_income}) \\
&\quad + 0.3268(\text{OWNERSHIP\_OTHER}) + 0.1362(\text{OWNERSHIP\_OWN}) + 0.1127(\text{OWNERSHIP\_RENT}) \\
&\quad + 3.6334(\text{GradeB}) + 6.0855(\text{GradeC}) + 7.9699(\text{GradeD}) \\
&\quad + 9.6154(\text{GradeE}) + 11.1983(\text{GradeF}) + 12.8389(\text{GradeG}) \\
&\quad + 0.0000075(\text{loan\_amnt}) - 0.3371(\text{loan\_percent\_income}) + 0.0081(\text{cred\_hist\_length})
\end{aligned}
$$
```{r}
b <- coef(current_model)


# Assisted Visualization with AI

impact_df <- tibble(
  Factor = c(
    "Loan Grade: G (vs. A)",
    "Loan Grade: F (vs. A)",
    "Loan Grade: E (vs. A)",
    "Loan Grade: D (vs. A)",
    "Loan Grade: C (vs. A)",
    "Loan Grade: B (vs. A)",
    "Home Ownership: Other (vs. Mortgage)",
    "Home Ownership: Own (vs. Mortgage)",
    "Home Ownership: Rent (vs. Mortgage)",
    "Credit History (+10 Years)",
    "Loan Amount (+$10,000)",
    "Person Income (+$25,000)",
    "Loan Percent Income (+10%)",
    "Borrower Age (+20 Years)"
  ),
  Change_Label = c(
    "Grade A → G", "Grade A → F", "Grade A → E",
    "Grade A → D", "Grade A → C", "Grade A → B",
    "Mortgage → Other", "Mortgage → Own", "Mortgage → Rent",
    "+10 years credit history", "+$10,000 borrowed",
    "+$25,000 annual income", "+0.10 loan-to-income ratio", "+20 years older"
  ),
  Rate_Shift = round(c(
    b["loan_gradeG"],
    b["loan_gradeF"],
    b["loan_gradeE"],
    b["loan_gradeD"],
    b["loan_gradeC"],
    b["loan_gradeB"],
    b["person_home_ownershipOTHER"],
    b["person_home_ownershipOWN"],
    b["person_home_ownershipRENT"],
    b["cb_person_cred_hist_length"] * 10,
    b["loan_amnt"] * 10000,
    b["person_income"] * 25000,
    b["loan_percent_income"] * 0.10,
    b["person_age"] * 20
  ), 3),
  Significance_Type = c(
    rep("Practically & Statistically Significant", 6),
    rep("Statistically Significant Only (Negligible Effect)", 8)
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>Factor:</b> ", Factor, "<br>",
      "<b>Scenario:</b> ", Change_Label, "<br>",
      "<b>Interest Rate Change:</b> ", ifelse(Rate_Shift >= 0, "+", ""), Rate_Shift, " percentage points"
    )
  )

p_all <- ggplot(
  impact_df,
  aes(x = reorder(Factor, Rate_Shift), y = Rate_Shift, fill = Significance_Type, text = hover_text)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, alpha = 0.92) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#2C3E50", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = paste0(ifelse(Rate_Shift >= 0, "+", ""), round(Rate_Shift, 2), "%"),
      hjust = ifelse(Rate_Shift >= 0, -0.15, 1.15)
    ),
    size = 3.2,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#1A2530"
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Practically & Statistically Significant" = "#2B5C8F",
      "Statistically Significant Only (Negligible Effect)" = "#E67E22"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(ifelse(x > 0, "+", ""), x, "%"),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.12, 0.18))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Final Model: Real-World Impact of Every Significant Predictor",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Change in Predicted Interest Rate (Percentage Points)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 24) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, color = "#1A2530"),
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#2C3E50"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#2C3E50", size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top"
  )

ggplotly(p_all, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(
    title = list(
      text = paste0(
        "<b>Final Model: Real-World Impact of Every Significant
        Predictor</b><br>"
      ),
      x = 0.01,
      y = 0.96,
      font = list(size = 15, color = "#1A2530")
    ),
    legend = list(
      orientation = "h",
      x = 0.01,
      y = 1.07,
      font = list(size = 11),
      title = list(text = "")
    ),
    xaxis = list(title = list(font = list(size = 12))),
    margin = list(t = 110, b = 55, l = 10, r = 20)
  )

```
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
As you can see, the only genuine practically significant factor is the loan_grade.

If you move down the credit tiers from Grade A to Grade G the predicted interest rates are increased by 3.63% (from Grade A to Grade B) up to 12.84% (Grade A to Grade G) which essentially dominates the entire model.

You can see that the orange bars are statistically significant but not practically significant at all.
The most statistically but not practically significant factor is Home Ownership, which is maxed out around 0.33%. This does not contribute a lot to the model.

If you were to take out a $15,000 loan for three years with a 7.33% interest rate vs a 7.00%, you would be paying around 80 more dollars, which isn't too much of an increase.
:::
